ticket.title: Add [telemetry] enabled with env-wins precedence
ticket.description:
ADR 0012 decided telemetry is switched off at runtime, with precedence env -> config -> default(true). The env half exists (GAUGEBLOCK_NO_TELEMETRY, GB-340); this is the config half.

Add [telemetry] with an `enabled` key to .gaugeblock/config.toml and consult it in gaugeblock_workspace::telemetry::emission_enabled, so the check stays in the one choke point every emitter already goes through rather than being repeated per tool.

WHY THIS AND NOT A CARGO FEATURE, restated because it will be asked again: cargo features are additive. A downstream crate cannot switch one off - default-features = false only declines what the consumer would have enabled, and any other crate in the graph re-enables it. So a feature gate would look like an opt-out for exactly the case that motivates it (someone installing one tool) and would not be one. It would also save nothing: spans are contract types (ADR 0002), so uuid, serde and serde_json are already in the graph.

DEFAULT true, deliberately. The honest cost is a directory a panel-less user never reads, bounded by rotation (GB-341); the honest benefit is that first_diagnostic records what failed on a lone tool with no benchwork installed, which is a real use the panel does not cover.

TESTS: config false disables emission; env set disables emission even when config says true (precedence); absent config or absent key means enabled; and emission_enabled stays false in a test binary regardless of config, since GB-340 established that a test must not write the production log.

DEPENDS: GB-338 gives the writer one location, so the config is read from the same place it writes.
